newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel sending peace envoy to U.S. with "ideas".
newsitem.headline: Israel sending peace envoy to U.S. with "ideas".

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Monday he was sending a senior adviser to Washington with proposals for ending a four-month-old peacemaking crisis with Palestinians.

"We are working jointly with the Americans and we have some bridging ideas. I believe they're good proposals," a spokesman quoted Netanyahu as telling members of the ruling Likud faction in parliament. He did not elaborate on the ideas.

"I have decided to send Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh, who coordinates the Palestinian issue for me, to Washington for meetings with Dennis Ross and others," Netanyahu said. Ross is a special U.S. Middle East envoy.

Israeli-PLO talks, launched with a U.S.-backed interim accord in 1993, have been stuck since Netanyahu started building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March, triggering Palestinian protests.

On Saturday, Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said Washington was preparing a "package deal" of measures to end the deadlock. But Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat said on Sunday there were as yet no new U.S. initiatives.

Netanyahu again demanded on Monday that Arafat's Palestinian Authority investigate allegations that senior security officials sent three police officers, now in Israeli custody, to attack Jews in the West Bank.

In the West Bank, Palestinian police said they had uncovered ready-to-use explosives and disguises at an apartment near Bethlehem which they suspected was a bomb lab of the anti-Israeli Hamas movement.

Netanyahu has demanded that Palestinians do more to crack down on Moslem guerrilla groups opposed to Israeli-PLO peace accords. "I would want to see these efforts done continuously," the Israeli leader said.

Bethlehem area police found Jewish religious skullcaps and prayer shawls and Israeli army uniforms in the apartment. Suicide bombers and kidnappers have posed as Israelis to carry out attacks which have killed scores of people in Israel.

Arafat was due to fly on Tuesday to Belgium where a PLO official said he would likely meet Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy to try to break the Middle East stalemate during a meeting of the 15-member European Union's foreign ministers.

In the Gaza Strip, a committee appointed by Arafat to investigate corruption recommended on Monday he put his house in order and that some senior officials be put on trial. The report was not made public and none of the names was disclosed.
But Majid al-Muzainy, a committee member and judge of the high justice court, said a cabinet reshuffle was expected soon after Arafat studied the committee recommendations.
"We have found serious financial, legal and administrative violations and flaws, some resulting from lack of experience," said Tayeb Abdel-Rahim, head of the presidential committee on corruption.

The committee, set up by Arafat in June, followed up on an official auditor's report which found that members of the ruling Palestinian Authority had squandered $326 million in public funds last year.
Israeli opposition leader Ehud Barak flew to Amman on Monday on a surprise visit at the invitation of Jordan's King Hussein, who has also been looking for ways to end the crisis.

Netanyahu, who has angered the king with his right-wing policies on Jerusalem and Jewish settlements, resists the peace deals that Barak's Labour party signed with Arafat based on the principle of land-for-peace.

Asked by Israel's Channel Two television why the meeting was so urgent, Barak said: "It reflects the depth of concern among regional leaders over the fact that the process is slipping between our fingers...and could deteriorate to violence."
